title: Export generated creatures as standard glTF/GLB with skeleton and skinning
description:
## Summary
Provide a standard, shareable export path for a generated creature that preserves the rest mesh, skeleton hierarchy, bone ordering, bind poses, vertex skin weights, submeshes/material assignments, and mirrored identities. Prefer glTF 2.0 / GLB so an exported artifact can be inspected independently of Unity and shared for debugging or review.

## User requirement
The exported artifact should be simple enough to share with external reviewers and should contain the information needed to inspect animation binding, not merely a static mesh.

## Scope
- Export the generated implicit surface through the existing resolved `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer`/binding data path.
- Export the resolved skeleton hierarchy and rest transforms in stable semantic/index order.
- Export up to the existing four influences per vertex with normalized weights.
- Export bind poses / equivalent glTF inverse-bind matrices.
- Preserve submeshes and material slots where glTF supports the source information without introducing a custom runtime format.
- Preserve mirrored bone identity and deterministic ordering.
- Provide a deterministic editor command/API that writes a `.glb` or `.gltf` plus required resources.
- Keep export build-time/editor-time only; never add export work to animation ticks or procedural generation hot paths.
- Add an optional diagnostic companion JSON containing CreatureCreator semantic IDs and task/audit metadata if this can be done without contaminating the standard glTF payload.

## Non-goals
- Do not create a proprietary CreatureCreator interchange format as the primary export.
- Do not add animation locomotion/state-machine logic.
- Do not regenerate geometry or recalculate weights during export if the generated/binding result already contains them.
- Do not make glTF a dependency of the runtime animation hot path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A real generated creature such as `dinus_uprightus` exports successfully.
- The exported mesh matches the generated rest geometry within the established tolerance.
- The exported skeleton contains the same semantic bone count/order/parenting and rest transforms as `SkeletonSnapshot`.
- The exported skin weights match the binding data and retain the four-influence ceiling.
- Importing the GLB into a standard glTF viewer shows the creature intact and skinned; a controlled bone pose deforms the mesh in the expected region.
- Mirrored limb deformation remains isolated and correct in the exported artifact.
- Export does not mutate the source mesh or creature definition.
- Export is deterministic for the same generated creature/binding input.
- No per-frame/runtime dependency on the exporter exists.

## Validation
Use a real generated creature and compare exported rest mesh/skeleton/weights against `GeneratedCreature`, `SkeletonSnapshot`, and `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer` binding data. Validate with at least one external glTF viewer or importer plus automated structural checks. Run dotnet builds and relevant Unity editor tests; measure export time separately from per-frame animation.

## Ownership
Child of the animation/presentation workstream. The exporter consumes existing binding data; it does not become a second source of skeleton/weight truth.

## Status
Backlog.

## Notes
The first implementation may target GLB only, provided it remains standards-compliant and contains mesh + skin + joints + inverse bind matrices in one shareable file.
